expect:
Mastering: Identifies that a higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles per second, improving throughput. However, increasing clock speed alone has diminishing returns: it generates more heat, can cause stability issues, and the CPU may still be bottlenecked by RAM access speeds (the bus transfers data at a fixed rate regardless of clock speed). Other factors also affect performance — for example, the number of cores allows parallel processing of independent tasks, and larger on-chip cache reduces the frequency of slow RAM accesses. Concludes that clock speed is one of several factors; the best improvement depends on the workload.
Secure: Identifies clock speed as increasing cycles per second, notes at least one limitation, and mentions one other performance factor (e.g. cores or cache) with some explanation.
Developing: Explains that faster clock means more operations per second; mentions one other factor without development.
Emerging: States clock speed affects performance; little or no development.
value:
Mastering: A higher clock speed means more pulses per second, so the CPU can start more fetch-decode-execute cycles each second and work through instructions faster. However, a faster clock alone has limits: it generates more heat and can make the processor unstable. The CPU also has to fetch every instruction and every data item from RAM along the buses, and RAM is much slower than the CPU, so the processor can end up waiting for data however fast the clock runs. Concludes that clock speed is only one factor, and that how quickly instructions and data reach the CPU from main memory matters as well.
Secure: Explains that a faster clock means more cycles per second, gives at least one limitation (heat, instability, or waiting for RAM), and reaches a judgement.
Developing: Explains that a faster clock means more operations per second and mentions one limitation without development.
Emerging: States that clock speed affects performance, with little or no development.
note: F2: cache and cores are not in this specification; replaced with on-spec limits (heat, instability, waiting on RAM across the buses).
